editorial.headline: Cultural Education Is Open Nationally—and Not Barred in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85520 covers structured, non-credential cultural training, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block on the recorded position.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85520 is the home for structured cultural education: teaching in music, visual arts, dance, drama, fine art, performing arts and photography, delivered through schools, studios, classes or similar settings. What gives the activity its shape is not simply the subject matter but the learning format. It is organised training, built around deliberate interaction between participant and instructor, and designed to support the training process. Its natural purposes are hobby, recreation and personal development. It does not confer qualifications within basic-to-tertiary education—a boundary that keeps the category focused on non-credential cultural learning rather than formal educational attainment. That distinction matters for a founder defining the offer. A music studio, dance class, art workshop or photography course belongs here when it is structured learning for those purposes, with a teacher and participants at the centre of the experience. The code is about teaching as a service—an arrangement in which lessons, instruction and practice have an intentional place.

Registration is open across the full scale spectrum recorded for this activity: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth is a practical clue to the code's reach. The same core proposition can be organised as a modest class-based practice or as a larger education business; the description remains anchored in structured cultural training rather than in the size or setting of the operator. The scales are not a grading of the teaching itself. They show stated registration openness from Micro through Large, while the core activity remains the same. Nationally, the investment position is unambiguous in the record: the activity is open to foreign investment, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put plainly, a foreign investor is not nationally required by this code to give up an ownership share merely because the activity is cultural education.

Bali is where the regional rule must be read without euphemism. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, island-wide. Yet this activity is not marked as blocked by that moratorium. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Large scale as Medium-High/High and expressly says that it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign investor examining KBLI 85520 in Bali today, the practical conclusion is clear: the regional restriction does not bar the activity on the record presented. The national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the relevant ceiling. The evidence is specific to the recorded risk position at Large scale; it should not be turned into a claim that Bali's moratorium has disappeared or that every cultural-training proposal is treated alike. It means that, for this activity as recorded, the regional restriction does not prevent PMA registration.
